title: Choose the visual world for KoLearn
question: The roll assigned The Red Sheet, built around the Kolearn logo's teal and blush. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Red Sheet
options.lineage: Korean study notebooks and the translucent red memorization sheet (암기 시트)
options.thesis: Reading is a highlighter pass; meanings hide under a translucent sheet until you lift it.
options.viewport: Phone Home: today's Naver article in large Hangul, key words highlighted, tap-and-hold a word to lift the red sheet and reveal its English.
options.risk: Sheet metaphor turns into decoration if reveal is not a real, repeatable interaction.

raised.raise: Hangul sets at specimen scale against tiny labels; hierarchy comes from size contrast alone.
Home shows one next action as the single dominant band, not a dashboard of stats.

regions.label: article, Hangul at display size, highlights

options.label: Wongoji Manuscript
options.lineage: 원고지 Korean manuscript paper, one syllable per square
options.thesis: Every Hangul syllable sits in its own square, the way Korean children learn to write.
options.viewport: Phone Translate: the Korean output set in a syllable grid under the English input.
options.risk: Grid can crowd body text; also the most obvious Hangul-learning idea.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.thesis: Hangul as the designed alphabet it is, shown at monumental scale with tiny UI labels.
options.viewport: One giant syllable, weight slider, grid of related syllables below.
options.case: Holds audience identification (Hangul's design is a draw); loses on clarity because it is a specimen, not a reading app.
options.risk: Becomes a type toy that hides the news and translate tasks.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.case: Yellow bands lose both axes: learners do not identify with transit signage and it hides reading content.
options.kept: One dominant next decision per screen.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.case: Loses both axes: articles are text, and a snap feed fights careful reading.
options.kept: One item owns the screen at a time.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.case: Loses both axes: travel-ticket nostalgia is unrelated to learning Korean.
options.kept: Used items stamp themselves instead of disappearing.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.case: Loses both axes: replaces native navigation with a panorama, which breaks platform rules.
options.kept: Total color commitment on live states.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.case: Loses both axes: dance notation has no tie to reading Korean.
options.kept: Time and length encoded in one clear axis.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean Duolingo-style learning app, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, streak, lesson cards, native tab bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from other language apps by design.
